//: Typecheck the dogfood files C4 owns.
WHY THIS EXISTS. The root tsconfig references only `packages/*`, so nothing under
`dogfood/` was ever typechecked, and `npx tsx` does not typecheck either. In one
phase of C4 that gap produced FOUR separate defects that all looked like working
code: a read of `zone.entryGate` on a type with no such field (which printed
'gates 0' for a world authoring three), two illegal `EntityRole` values that
crashed a converter, a MarketNode built from invented field names that crashed
another, and a missing required `hidden` that made the emitted .tscn unparseable
by Godot.
WAVE-2 UPDATE (F-007 / F-7c6f2616-family). The 2-file scope above was itself named
as a live gap: it had grown from 3 affected files (per the original note below) to
6, unmonitored, and was hiding two real bugs (F-008: multi-target-export-proof.ts's
`f.field` should be `f.fieldPath`; F-009: run-ai-rpg-smoke.ts's `new Engine(...)`
should be `new EngineClass(...)`). Both fixed. The `import.meta` blocker (TS1470,
'not allowed in files which will build into CommonJS output') was a project-
configuration mismatch, not a content bug: these files run via `tsx` as ESM, but
`module: NodeNext` classified them as CommonJS because the root package.json has
no `type: module` (root package.json is outside this domain's scope to change).
Switching to `module: ESNext` / `moduleResolution: Bundler` matches how tsx
actually executes these files and clears every import.meta error with no content
changes. 9 of 10 dogfood/*.ts files are now covered — every one that was previously
excluded except run-ai-rpg-smoke.ts, which needed real work (a bare-specifier import
fix — it hardcoded a relative path into node_modules that only tsc's relative-file
resolution, unlike Node's own runtime resolution, cannot follow — plus filling in a
RulesetDefinition object that was missing every field the real type requires) and is
now included too. 10 of 10.
Not yet wired into `npm run build`/`verify`/`prebuild` — those are root package.json
scripts, outside this domain's owned globs (dogfood/**, e2e/**, scripts/**, taste/**,
vitest.*.ts, playwright.config.ts, tsconfig*.json). Flagged for whichever domain owns
root package.json (ci-tooling, going by this swarm's domain map) to wire
`typecheck:dogfood` into `verify` or `prebuild` so this protection stops being opt-in.
WHY IT WAS ORIGINALLY SCOPED TO TWO FILES. Pointing this at the whole tree surfaced
pre-existing errors in five files that had nothing to do with that cycle: `import.meta`
under a CommonJS module setting in three of them, a `FidelityEntry.field` that no
longer exists, and a ContentPack variance mismatch in run-ai-rpg-smoke. Fixing those
was real work and somebody's cycle, not a detour inside that one. ANDON: named, not
silently widened. (That 'somebody's cycle' is this one.)
It earned its keep on the first run, finding two more live bugs in the file it was
written for: `packFormatVersion` (the field is `formatVersion`) and `zone.name`
(it is `displayName`), both silently emitting nothing into every generated fixture.
Run with: npm run typecheck:dogfood
